Mikhail Gorbachev: Born in Privolnoye, North Caucasus Krai, into a peasant family of Russian and Ukrainian heritage, Gorbachev grew up under the rule of Joseph Stalin.

Waco siege: United States. The ATF had planned a sudden daylight raid of the ranch in order to serve these warrants.

Battle of Gaza (2007): Palestine. The Battle of Gaza, also known as the Gaza civil war, was a brief civil war between Fatah and Hamas that took place in the Gaza Strip from 7 to 15 June 2007.

Siege of Turin: Italy. The Siege of Turin, June to September 1706, took place during the War of the Spanish Succession.

British Union of Fascists: United Kingdom. The British Union of Fascists (BUF) was a British fascist political party formed in 1932 by Oswald Mosley.
Which of these was an official language of the Vijayanagara Empire?
Vijayanagara Empire: Kannada. The Vijayanagara Empire, also known as the Karnata Empire, was a late medieval Hindu empire that ruled much of southern India.
Which of these was an official language of the Kingdom of Mysore?
Kingdom of Mysore: Kannada. The Kingdom of Mysore was a geopolitical realm in southern India founded in around 1399 in the vicinity of the modern-day city of Mysuru and prevailed until 1950.

Golden Horde: Turki. It is also known as the Kipchak Khanate, and replaced the earlier, less organized Cuman–Kipchak confederation.

The Yugoslav krone is the official currency of Kingdom of Yugoslavia. The Kingdom of Yugoslavia was a country in Southeast and Central Europe that existed from 1918 until 1941.
Fill in the blank: “____ are a Fatah-aligned coalition of Palestinian armed groups in the West Bank and the Gaza Strip.”

Al-Aqsa Martyrs' Brigades are a Fatah-aligned coalition of Palestinian armed groups in the West Bank and the Gaza Strip. The al-Aqsa Martyrs' Brigades have conducted various armed attacks on Israeli military and civilian targets since 2000.

This political theory leans heavily on the "non-aggression principle" to argue that even policing, courts, and defense could be supplied by private providers in a wholly voluntary society. What's this stateless ideology called?

Anarcho-capitalism (colloquially: ANCAP, Ancap, AnCap, or An-Cap) is a political ideology and economic theory that advocates for the abolition of state monopolies and promotes their replacement with private providers.
A senior Supreme Court advocate who led the opposition in India's Rajya Sabha from 2009 to 2014, this BJP leader later steered the country's finance ministry through demonetisation — who is he?
Arun Jaitley (28 December 1952 - 24 August 2019) was an Indian politician and attorney.

Fought in 657 CE on the banks of the Euphrates, this clash pitted the fourth Rashidun caliph, Ali ibn Abi Talib, against a rebelling Levantine governor, ending in arbitration after Ali gained the upper hand — which battle?

Battle of Siffin was fought in 657 CE (37 AH) between the Iraqi Arab forces of the fourth Rashidun caliph Ali ibn Abi Talib and the Syrian Arab forces of the rebelling long-time governor of the Levant, Mu'awiya ibn Abi Sufyan.
A mechanic and trade unionist from León radicalized by state repression, he became a celebrated anarchist militant and martyr of the Spanish Civil War — who was he?
Buenaventura Durruti (14 July 1896 - 20 November 1936) was a Spanish anarcho-syndicalist militant and a leading figure in Spanish anarchism before and during the Spanish Civil War.
He began ruling Neustria as an infant under his mother's regency, then settled a long royal feud by having Queen Brunhilda executed by dismemberment in 613 — which king of the Franks was he?
Chlothar II (May/June 584 - 18 October 629) was king of the Franks, ruling Neustria (584-629), Burgundy (613-629) and Austrasia (613-623).

This Nicaraguan revolutionary and former guerrilla fighter first led his country as coordinator of a reconstruction junta starting in 1979, then served as president until 1990, before reclaiming power again in 2007 — who is he?

Daniel Ortega (or-,; born 11 November 1945) is a Nicaraguan politician, revolutionary, and former guerrilla fighter who, under various titles, has been the leader of Nicaragua since 2007 and previously from 1979 to 1990.

This book of Hebrew Bible wisdom literature opens with 'the words of the Preacher, son of David, king in Jerusalem' — its English title comes via Latin from a Greek translation of a Hebrew word. Name the book?
Ecclesiastes (ih-) is one of the Ketuvim ('Writings') of the Hebrew Bible and part of the wisdom literature of the Christian Old Testament.

This American public servant served as White House cabinet secretary under President Biden, after earlier working as an assistant to Biden when he was vice president and as a State Department official under Obama. Who is she?
Evan Ryan is an American public servant who served as White House cabinet secretary in the administration of Joe Biden.
This Congolese politician became his country's fifth president in 2019, succeeding his own late father as leader of the nation's oldest and largest political party. Who is he?
Félix Tshisekedi (born 13 June 1963) is a Congolese politician who is the fifth president of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, serving since 2019.
Ending with the Ottoman Empire's first major territorial losses in Hungary and the Balkans, this late-17th-century conflict was settled by the 1699 Treaty of Karlowitz — which conflict?
Great Turkish War was a series of conflicts between the Ottoman Empire and the Holy League consisting of the Holy Roman Empire, Poland-Lithuania, Venice, Russia, and the Kingdom of Hungary.
Across many religions and folklore, this afterlife destination is where souls face punishment after death — sometimes forever, sometimes only until the next incarnation — what is it?
Hell is a location or state in the afterlife in which souls are subjected to punishment after death.

Born a peasant in 1916 and working as a humble schoolmaster, this man slowly built such influence among the uneducated that he rose to lead Dahomey — today's Benin — into independence from France. Who was he?
Hubert Maga (August 10, 1916 - May 8, 2000) was a politician from Dahomey (now known as Benin).
Before becoming her country's 40th prime minister in 2017, this Hamilton-raised leader once worked as a researcher for Helen Clark and advised Tony Blair's Cabinet Office in London. Who is she?
Jacinda Ardern (ah-DURN; born 26 July 1980) is a former New Zealand politician and activist who was the 40th prime minister of New Zealand and leader of the Labour Party from 2017 to 2023.
A two-time NCAA national champion wrestler and former college coach, this Ohio congressman helped found the right-wing House Freedom Caucus, serving as its first chair — who is he?
Jim Jordan (born February 17, 1964) is an American politician who has served in the U.S.
Serving as Gauleiter of Franconia and founding a virulently antisemitic Nazi newspaper, this German publicist and politician was convicted as a war criminal — who was he?
Julius Streicher (12 February 1885 - 16 October 1946) was a German publicist, politician, and convicted war criminal.

Traditionally founded in 843 and occupying the northern third of the island of Great Britain, this sovereign kingdom fought England for its independence and later annexed the Hebrides and Northern Isles from Norway — which kingdom?
Kingdom of Scotland was a sovereign state in northwest Europe, traditionally said to have been founded in 843.

General Leclerc's 2nd French Armored Division reached the Hôtel de Ville just before midnight on 24 August 1944, a day before the German garrison surrendered this occupied capital — what event was this?
Liberation of Paris was a battle that took place during World War II from 19 August 1944 until the German garrison surrendered the French capital on 25 August 1944.
The eldest son of the founder of the People's Republic of China, this officer was educated in Moscow and died in a napalm strike during the Korean War — who was he?
Mao Anying (pinyin: Mo nyng; 24 October 1922 - 25 November 1950) was a Chinese military officer.
According to the Iliad, this king of Sparta's wife Helen fled to Troy with the prince Paris, sparking the Trojan War in which he led the Spartan contingent under his brother Agamemnon — who is he?
Menelaus (Ancient) was a king of Sparta. Menelaus was a central figure in the Trojan War, leading the Spartan contingent of the Greek army, under his elder brother Agamemnon, king of Mycenae.
Trained in Islamic theology in Qom and a veteran of the Iran–Iraq War, this cleric served as Vakil of the Supreme Leader before succeeding his father atop Iran's clerical hierarchy — who is he?
Mojtaba Khamenei (born 8 September 1969) is an Iranian cleric and politician who has served as the third supreme leader of Iran since 2026.
Before a north-Atlanta district sent him to Congress, this future House Speaker taught history and geography at the University of West Georgia — who went from professor to the 50th Speaker?
Newt Gingrich (born Newton Leroy McPherson; born June 17, 1943) is an American politician who served as the 50th speaker of the United States House of Representatives from 1995 to 1999.
This Italian journalist and former WWII resistance member wrote Interview with History, collecting her famously combative sit-downs with leaders like Yasser Arafat and Willy Brandt — who is she?
Oriana Fallaci (29 June 1929 - 15 September 2006) was an Italian journalist and author.

This seafaring Semitic people clung to a thin strip of Canaanite coast — from Arwad to Mount Carmel, in today's Lebanon and Syria — yet seeded colonies from Cyprus to Iberia and left thousands of inscriptions behind. Which Mediterranean civilization was it?
Phoenicia were an ancient Semitic people who inhabited city-states in Canaan along the Levantine coast of the eastern Mediterranean, primarily in present-day Lebanon and parts of coastal Syria.
Falling in the ninth month of the Islamic calendar, this observance asks the faithful to fast from dawn to sunset — though travelers, the ill, and the pregnant are excused — what is it?

Ramadan is the ninth month of the Islamic calendar. It is observed by Muslims worldwide as a month of fasting (sawm), communal prayer (salah), reflection, study of the Quran, charity, and strengthening community ties.

The founder of Electronic Data Systems mounted independent and third-party runs for president in 1992 and 1996 that, despite winning no states, ranked among the strongest in U.S. history — who was this Texan businessman?
Ross Perot (p-ROH; June 27, 1930 - July 9, 2019) was an American businessman, politician, and philanthropist.

Carved out in 312 BC by one of Alexander the Great's generals after his empire's breakup, this Hellenistic Greek state stretched across the Near East until Rome's Pompey annexed it in 63 BC — which empire?
Seleucid Empire (sih-) was a Greek state in West Asia during the Hellenistic period.
Bookended by winter and summer, this temperate season opens with an equinox that splits day and night nearly evenly before daylight steadily lengthens — which season is it?
Spring (season) is one of the four temperate seasons, succeeding winter and preceding summer.
Born from 1980s doubts about interventionist economics, this synthesis of center-right and center-left ideas favors 'hand-up' programs over traditional welfare — what's it called?

Third Way is a predominantly centrist political position that attempts to reconcile centre-right and centre-left politics by synthesising a combination of economically liberal and social democratic economic policies.

This Roman emperor, the last to emerge victorious from the chaotic Year of the Four Emperors, founded the Flavian dynasty and launched an extensive building program during his decade-long reign — who was he?
Vespasian (17 November 9 AD - 23 June 79) was Roman emperor from 69 to 79.
This U.S. president died just 31 days into his term, making him both the shortest-serving president and the first to die in office. Who is he?
William Henry Harrison (February 9, 1773 - April 4, 1841) was the ninth president of the United States from March to April 1841.
Born into poverty but educated thanks to a wealthy uncle, this Chinese general commanded the Eighth Route Army and is counted among the principal founders of the People's Republic. Who was he?
Zhu De (1 December 1886 - 6 July 1976) was a Chinese general, military strategist, politician and revolutionary in the Chinese Communist Party (CCP).
Allegedly the first Syrian to hold the position, this militant leader served as the fourth so-called caliph of the Islamic State from November 2022 until his death in April 2023. Who was he?
Abu al-Hussein al-Husseini al-Qurashi: Islamic State leader from 2022 to 2023.
An Iranic nomadic people connected to the Yancai and Aorsi of ancient sources, this group dominated the Pontic-Caspian steppe before the Goths broke their hold in the 3rd century CE — who were they?
Alans: Ancient Iranic people of the North Caucasus.
Formed in 1993 by merging a party from West Germany with one from East Germany, this party held 85 of the Bundestag's 630 seats after Germany's 2025 election — which party?
Alliance 90/The Greens: Green political party in Germany.
Never formally declared, this intermittent conflict saw England repel one armada in 1588 while Spain repelled a counter-armada the very next year, all amid relentless privateering. Which war was it?
Anglo-Spanish War (1585–1604): War between the kingdoms of Spain and England.
Governing Japan from Kyoto during the Muromachi period, this feudal military government ran from 1336 to 1573 and began after overthrowing the Kenmu Restoration — which regime?

Ashikaga shogunate: Ruling military government of feudal Japan (1336–1573). The Ashikaga clan governed Japan from the Imperial capital of Heian-kyō (Kyoto) as de facto military rulers along with the daimyō lords of the samurai class.
Serving as Poland's Minister of National Education since December 2023, she is the daughter of a former Polish Deputy Prime Minister who oversaw social policy — who is she?
Born in Montevideo during his father's exile, this Guatemalan sociologist-turned-politician co-founded the Semilla party and became his country's president in 2024 — who is he?
Bernardo Arévalo: President of Guatemala since 2024.
This 19th-century religious leader served as the second president of a major American church and doubled as the first governor of Utah Territory. Who is he?

This ancient state, whose territory mostly overlapped modern Azerbaijan, gets its Western name from a Greek mistranslation of an Armenian term — which historical realm is this, whose descendants include the Udi people?

Caucasian Albania: Ancient state in the Caucasus. Caucasian Albania is a modern exonym for a former state located in ancient times in the Caucasus, mostly overlapping the region of present-day Azerbaijan.
Mentally ill for most of his reign, this 18th-century Danish-Norwegian king let his court physician rule as a de facto dictator from 1770 to 1772 before a coup deposed the doctor — who was the king?
Christian VII: King of Denmark and Norway from 1766 to 1808.

Named for the Latin word for 'body,' this political ideology has trade and professional associations bargain collectively with government, advocating cooperation between classes rather than struggle between them — what is it?
Corporatism: Political ideology which advocates the organization of society by corporate groups.
This Scottish officer founded the Special Air Service and led hit-and-run raids behind Axis lines in North Africa during World War II — who is he?

David Stirling: Scottish World War II officer, and founder of the Special Air Service. Stirling's preference for a limited, elitist voting franchise over universal suffrage limited the movement's appeal.
The younger brother of Titus and last ruler of the Flavian dynasty, this Roman emperor's 15-year reign was the longest since Tiberius — who was he?
Domitian: Roman emperor from AD 81 to 96.
His brief 1982–83 turn as Guatemala's de facto president became one of the bloodiest chapters of its civil war, later drawing accusations of genocide — which former military academy director was he?
Efraín Ríos Montt: 38th President of Guatemala from 1982 to 1983.
In Greek mythology, this goddess of strife started a quarrel among Hera, Athena, and Aphrodite that led to the Judgement of Paris and, ultimately, the Trojan War — who is she?
Eris (mythology): Greek goddess of strife and discord. All of Eris' children are little more than allegorizations of the meanings of their names, with virtually no other identity.
The last man ever promoted to Field Marshal in the German military during World War II, this commander became notorious among his own troops for his brutal treatment of deserters — who was he?

Born from the coup of 18 Brumaire in 1799 and ending with the start of an empire in 1804, this government put Napoleon Bonaparte in charge as an authoritarian head of a still-nominal republic — what was it called?
French Consulate: Government of France from 1799 to 1804.
Becoming the first openly LGBTQ Republican elected to Congress as a freshman, this New York representative was expelled within a year after much of his biography proved fabricated — who is he?
George Santos: American politician and convicted felon (born 1988)
Trapped by an anticyclone and windless conditions in December 1952, this coal-fueled pollution event over England's capital killed an estimated 4,000 people in less than a week — what was it called?
Great Smog of London: 1952 air pollution event. It lasted from Friday, 5 December to Tuesday, 9 December 1952, then dispersed quickly when the weather changed.

A general, poet, and inventor of the Song dynasty, this commander was famed for winning battles against larger forces — and was said to have ended his career covered in scars with only four fingers left on his hands. Who was he?

This Welsh privateer raided Spanish settlements from his Port Royal base, then used the plunder to buy three Jamaican sugar plantations and eventually became the island's lieutenant governor — who was he?
Henry Morgan: Welsh privateer, politician in Jamaica (1635–1688)
Formed by the 1736 marriage of a French duke to Maria Theresa of Austria, this dynasty merged two royal lines, inheriting through the mother's family and the father's — which dynasty?
House of Habsburg-Lorraine: Austrian imperial dynasty.
This Ukrainian politician fled to Russia in 2022 and publicly backed its invasion of Ukraine, leading parliament to strip his mandate and Ukrainian courts to convict him of treason — who was he?
Educated at Al-Azhar and later a preacher in his native Jableh, this early-20th-century leader fought against French rule in Syria and British rule in Palestine — who was he?
Izz ad-Din al-Qassam: Syrian Muslim preacher (1882–1935)
After leading Taiwan's Environmental Protection Administration, this media personality co-founded the pro-unification New Party and ran for vice president on the KMT ticket in 2024 — who is he?
Jaw Shaw-kong: Taiwanese media personality and politician.
This North Carolina senator ran as the Democratic vice-presidential nominee alongside Kerry in 2004, after twice seeking his party's presidential nomination — who was he?
John Edwards: American lawyer and politician (born 1953)
Born in Roman exile and grandson of Alfonso XIII, this royal reigned over Spain from 1975 until abdicating in 2014, after which the press dubbed him the rey emérito — who is he?
Juan Carlos I: King of Spain from 1975 to 2014. In Spain, since his abdication, Juan Carlos has usually been referred to as the rey emérito ('king emeritus') by the press.

Emerging from the fragmentation of the Golden Horde around 1465, this Central Asian nomadic state eventually stretched from the Caspian and Aral seas to the Ural Mountains under Kasym Khan — what was it?
Kazakh Khanate: 1465–1847 Turkic state in Central Asia.
Roughly 100,000 prospectors stampeded toward Canada's Yukon after an 1896 strike, most braving the brutal Chilkoot or White Pass trails — a frenzy later immortalized in films and photographs as what?
Klondike Gold Rush: 1896–1899 migration to Yukon, Canada.
This political ideology calls for a revolutionary vanguard party to lead a "dictatorship of the proletariat" as the prelude to communism — what is it named for its Russian architect?
Leninism: Political theory developed by Vladimir Lenin.

Crowned in 844 and co-ruling with his father Lothair I until 855, this Carolingian emperor adopted the title 'emperor of the Romans' after conquering Bari in 871 — straining ties with Byzantium. Who was he?
Louis II of Italy: Ruler of the Carolingian Empire from 844 to 875.
Founded by Raden Wijaya in 1292, this Javanese Hindu-Buddhist empire once controlled nearly the entire Nusantara archipelago before collapsing in 1527 — what was it?
Majapahit: Javanese empire from 1292 to 1527. The fall of Majapahit saw the rise of Islamic kingdoms in Java.
The granddaughter of France's National Front founder and niece of the party's later leader, this politician became France's youngest parliamentarian in modern history at just 22 — who is she?
Crowned sultan twice — once as a boy, once as a man who built up the Ottoman navy — he earned a nickname meaning 'the Father of Conquest' — which ruler?
Mehmed II: Sultan of the Ottoman Empire (r. 1444–1446, 1451–1481)
Founding the Kamakura shogunate in 1192, this samurai became the first shogun to hold true nationwide power in Japan, having defeated the rival Taira clan in a five-year civil war — who is he?
Minamoto no Yoritomo: Japanese Samurai, Daimyo and Military ruler of Japan from 1192 to 1199.
Ruling a dynasty based in what is now central Afghanistan from 1173 to 1206, this figure extended his realm eastward into South Asia, ushering in centuries of Islamic rule there — who was he?
Muhammad of Ghor: Ghurid sultan from 1173 to 1206.

This South African anti-apartheid activist spent his revolutionary decades fighting to dismantle racial oppression, became the nation's first Black president in 1994, and spent his administration fostering reconciliation and building multiracial democracy. Who was he?
Nelson Mandela: President of South Africa from 1994 to 1999.
A Peronist who governed Argentina from 2003 to 2007, he later became the country's first 'first gentleman' when his wife succeeded him as president — who was he?

Néstor Kirchner: President of Argentina from 2003 to 2007. Néstor Carlos Kirchner Ostoić (25 February 1950 – 27 October 2010) was an Argentine lawyer and politician who served as the president of Argentina from 2003 to 2007.
Also called the Old Stone Age, this era of human prehistory stretched from the earliest known stone tools roughly 3.3 million years ago until about 11,650 years ago — which period is it?
Paleolithic: Prehistoric period, first part of the Stone Age.
A former army general who once chaired NATO's Military Committee, this politician became the Czech Republic's fourth president in 2023 — who is he?
Petr Pavel: President of the Czech Republic since 2023. Born in Planá to a military family, Pavel enlisted right after graduating from military academy in 1983.

Born a granddaughter of a Balkan king and later married to a British prince, she was widowed in 1942 when her husband died in a wartime plane crash, and spent her later years attending Commonwealth independence celebrations in Ghana and Botswana — who was this future Duchess of Kent?
Princess Marina of Greece and Denmark
Princess Marina of Greece and Denmark: Duchess of Kent (1906–1968)
Princess Marina of Greece and Denmark
This Kentucky senator, a practicing ophthalmologist before entering politics, is the son of a three-time presidential candidate and 12-term Texas congressman — who is he?
Condemned to death in 1553 after his family fell from power, this Englishman was released and later rose to become Elizabeth I's lifelong favourite and a long-time suitor for her hand — who was he?
Robert Dudley, 1st Earl of Leicester: English statesman (1532–1588)
A career diplomat turned politician, this BJP member rose from foreign secretary to become India's longest-serving minister to hold the External Affairs portfolio exclusively. Who is he?
S. Jaishankar: Indian diplomat and politician (born 1955)

His 1971 book "Rules for Radicals: A Pragmatic Primer" defended both confrontation and compromise, drawn from his work with Chicago's Industrial Areas Foundation organizing poor communities — which American activist wrote it?
Saul Alinsky: American activist and political theorist (1909–1972)
Known by the kunya Abu Idris, this Chechen guerrilla commander helped recapture Grozny in 1996 and later masterminded some of Russia's worst hostage-taking attacks — who is he?
Born in 1955, this Princess Royal of Thailand is the second daughter of King Bhumibol Adulyadej and the younger sister of King Vajiralongkorn — who is she?
Sirindhorn: Thai princess (born 1955). Maha Chakri Sirindhorn, The Princess Royal (born 2 April 1955) is a member of the Thai royal family.
His was the longest reign of any Ottoman sultan, taking Belgrade in 1521 and Rhodes in 1522 and shattering Hungary's army at Mohács in 1526 — who was this sultan?
Suleiman the Magnificent: Sultan of the Ottoman Empire (1520–1566)
Also called the Decalogue, these covenant directives were given to Moses atop Mount Sinai and later smashed after he found the Israelites worshipping a golden calf. What are they?
Ten Commandments: Biblical principles relating to ethics and worship.
Before ruling Rome from 79 to 81 AD, he commanded the siege that ended the Jewish rebellion — and became the first Roman emperor ever to directly succeed his own biological father; who was he?
Titus: Roman emperor from AD 79 to 81. Titus Flavius Vespasianus (30 December 39 – 13 September 81 AD) was Roman emperor from 79 to 81 AD.
Explicitly authorized by the Constitution, this independent government agency replaced a Cabinet department in 1971 and holds a legal monopoly on traditional letter delivery — which agency?
United States Postal Service: Independent agency of the U.S. federal government.

His brother was executed for revolutionary activities in 1887, pushing him toward radical politics. He founded the Bolsheviks, led the October Revolution, and created the world's first communist state—then ruled it until his death in 1924. Who was this Russian revolutionary?
Vladimir Lenin: Leader of the Soviet Union from 1922 to 1924.
Crowned King of Prussia in 1861, this Hohenzollern monarch became the first emperor of a unified Germany a decade later — who was he?
Wilhelm I: German Emperor from 1871 to 1888.
Founded in London in 1844 by George Williams to promote 'muscular Christianity,' this youth organization now serves over 64 million people worldwide?
YMCA: Worldwide youth organization. YMCA is a worldwide youth organization based in Vernier, Canton of Geneva, Switzerland, with more than 64 million beneficiaries in 120 countries.

This exaggerated immune reaction causes the body to mistake a harmless substance for a threat, triggering symptoms from a runny nose to a full anaphylactic reaction — what is it?
Allergy is an exaggerated immune response where the body mistakenly identifies an ordinarily harmless allergen as a threat.

Ant are eusocial insects of the family Formicidae and, along with the related wasps and bees, belong to the order Hymenoptera.
With atomic number 85 and symbol At, this is the rarest naturally occurring element in Earth's crust, forming only as a decay product of heavier elements — name it?
Astatine is a chemical element; it has symbol At and atomic number 85.
A civil-engineering graduate who first reshaped his father's firm toward real estate, this Frenchman now chairs the world's largest luxury goods company — who is he?

Native to South American tropical forests, this thorny ornamental vine, bush, or tree produces large colorful bracts surrounding three small waxy flowers — what is this plant genus?

Calorie is a unit of energy that originated from the caloric theory of heat.
This class of ribbon-like parasitic flatworms sheds egg-packed body segments called proglottids into the environment to infect new hosts — what is this class called (scientific name)?
Cestoda is a class of parasitic worms in the flatworm phylum (Platyhelminthes).
Once home to a bacterium behind a common cause of diarrhea before its 2016 reclassification, this genus of soil-dwelling bacteria also causes botulism — which genus?
Clostridium is a genus of anaerobic, Gram-positive bacteria.
Released on a daily cycle and spiking when you're stressed, this glucocorticoid raises blood sugar through gluconeogenesis and even tamps down the immune system — what stress hormone is it?
Cortisol is a steroid hormone in the glucocorticoid class of hormones and a stress hormone.
Marked by a telltale skin rash plus progressive muscle weakness, this systemic autoimmune condition can also bring fever, weight loss and light sensitivity — which disease?

Eagle is the common name for certain large birds of prey within the family of the Accipitridae.
This American investor and podcaster coined the phrase 'intellectual dark web' and proposed a physics framework called 'Geometric Unity' — who is he?
Eric Weinstein (born October 26, 1965) is an American investor and podcast host.

Native to the Indian subcontinent and Indochina, this fig species carries deep religious significance across four faiths that originated there, including reverence from Hindu and Jain ascetics — what species is it?
Ficus religiosa is a species of fig native to the Indian subcontinent and Indochina that belongs to Moraceae, the fig or mulberry family.
Found on every continent except Antarctica, this lizard lacks eyelids — instead its eyeballs are covered by a transparent membrane called a brille. What is it?
Gecko are small, mostly carnivorous lizards that have a wide distribution, found on every continent except Antarctica.
One of only two wild camelid species native to South America, this llama relative lives at lower elevations than its cousin, the vicuña — what is it called?
Guanaco (gwah-; Lama guanicoe) is a camelid native to South America, closely related to the domesticated llama.
Never approved by any drug regulator, this THC-like compound made by hydrogenating cannabis isomers has been sold in head-shop vaporizers since the early 2020s — what is it?
Hexahydrocannabinol (HHC) is a phytocannabinoid that has been reported as a minor component of Cannabis oleoresin.

Worldwide, too little dietary iodine is the leading cause of this endocrine condition, in which a sluggish thyroid leaves people cold-intolerant, exhausted, constipated, and prone to weight gain — what is it?
Hypothyroidism is an endocrine disease in which the thyroid gland does not produce enough thyroid hormones.
A Scottish surgeon who corrected clubfoot and squints, he's also dubbed by some the 'Father of Modern Hypnotism' — pioneering both hypnotic and chemical anaesthesia. Who was this gentleman scientist?
James Braid (surgeon) (19 June 1795 - 25 March 1860) was a Scottish surgeon, natural philosopher, and "gentleman scientist".
One species of this succulent plant genus, native mainly to Madagascar, became one of the first plants ever sent into space aboard a Soviet space station in 1979 — what genus is it?
Kalanchoe (also called "kalanche" or "kalancho"), is a genus of about 125 species of tropical, succulent plants in the stonecrop family Crassulaceae, mainly native to Madagascar and tropical Africa.

Spread by the bite of sandflies and caused by a genus of protozoal parasites, this tropical disease can present as skin ulcers, disfiguring mucosal damage, or a more dangerous internal form. Name the disease?
Leishmaniasis is a wide array of clinical manifestations caused by protozoal parasites of the Trypanosomatida genus Leishmania.
This evergreen tree, native to the cooler hills of south-central China, is grown commercially for its orange fruit and is sometimes called the Japanese medlar. What is it?
Loquat (Eriobotrya japonica) is a large evergreen shrub or tree grown commercially for its orange coloured fruits.
Following fieldwork with the Omaha people and in Papua New Guinea and Bali, this anthropologist explored gender roles in her 1935 book Sex and Temperament in Three Primitive Societies — who is she?
Margaret Mead (December 16, 1901 - November 15, 1978) was an American cultural anthropologist, author and speaker, who appeared frequently in the mass media during the mid-twentieth century.
Despite little formal education, this self-made English scientist established the concept of the electromagnetic field and uncovered the principles behind electromagnetic induction — who is he?
Michael Faraday (22 September 1791 - 25 August 1867) was an English chemist and physicist who contributed vastly to the study of electrochemistry and electromagnetism.
This group of more than 30 rare neuromuscular disorders causes skeletal tissue to progressively weaken and break down, differing in which body parts are hit first and how fast — what's it called?
Muscular dystrophy (MD) is a genetically and clinically heterogeneous group of rare neuromuscular diseases that cause progressive weakness and breakdown of skeletal muscles over time.
This raised region of tissue on the breast, surrounded by the darker-colored areola, is where milk exits the body through the lactiferous ducts during breastfeeding — name this body part?
Nipple is a raised region of tissue on the surface of the breast from which, in lactating females, milk from the mammary gland leaves the body through the lactiferous ducts to nurse an infant.
Usually caused by bacteria and sometimes requiring amputation in severe cases, this infectious inflammation of bone can be acute or chronic — which condition?
Osteomyelitis (OM) is the infectious inflammation of bone. It may be acute or chronic and can be classified as hematogenous or non-hematogenous.
Recognized by a long beak and an enormous throat pouch used to drain water from scooped-up prey before swallowing, these large water birds come in eight living species worldwide — which birds?
Pelican (genus Pelecanus) are a genus of large water birds that make up the family Pelecanidae.
What small, tailless, round-bodied mountain mammal — a close relative of the rabbit with short rounded ears — includes a large-eared Himalayan species that lives above 6,000 meters?
Pika is a small, mountain-dwelling mammal native to Asia and North America.
Lacking any real scientific definition, this British term for a large swimming crustacean has become almost interchangeable with 'shrimp' — what is it?
Prawn is a common name for small aquatic crustaceans with an exoskeleton and ten legs (members of the order of decapods), some of which are edible.
A zoonotic virus that triggers violent movements, a dread of water, and almost certain death once symptoms set in — usually one to three months after exposure. What is this disease?
Rabies is a zoonotic viral disease that causes acute and severe encephalitis in humans and other mammals.
This British economist won the 1991 Nobel Memorial Prize and warned that the field was "suicidal" to become a hard science of choice while ignoring society, history, and culture — who was he?
Ronald Coase (29 December 1910 - 2 September 2013) was a British economist and author.
Which leathery-skinned marine echinoderm, of which about 1,786 species are known worldwide, plays a vital ecological role on the sea floor by breaking down detritus as a scavenger?
Sea cucumber are echinoderms from the class Holothuroidea.
Which urban model uses digital technology and data from citizens, buildings, and cameras to improve sustainability, efficiency, and social inclusion?
Smart city is an urban model that leverages technology, human capital, and governance to improve sustainability, efficiency, and social inclusion, which are considered goals for cities of the future.
Born in 1955, this former physician left medicine to pursue UFO research, founding an organization dedicated to studying extraterrestrial intelligence — who is he?
Steven M. Greer (born 1955) is an American ufologist and a retired physician.

Tellurium is a chemical element; it has the symbol Te and atomic number 52.
Dolphins, porpoises, beaked whales and sperm whales all belong to this cetacean group that diverged from baleen whales around 34 million years ago — what's the collective name?

Toothed whale (also called odontocetes, systematic name Odontoceti) are a parvorder of cetaceans that includes dolphins, porpoises, and all other whales with teeth, such as beaked whales and the sperm whales.

Amartya Sen: Indian economist and Nobel laureate (born 1933)

Ankylosaurus: Ankylosaurid dinosaur genus from the Late Cretaceous Period.
Native to the Philippines and spread by Austronesian voyagers as early as 1500 BCE, this palm's fruit is chewed with slaked lime and betel leaves for its stimulant effects — which species?
Areca catechu: Species of palm. It was carried widely through the tropics by the Austronesian migrations and trade since at least 1500 BCE due to its use in betel nut chewing.

Despite its name being something of a misnomer, this herding dog breed was developed in California and takes its name from imported collies that arrived alongside sheep from Down Under — what breed is it?
Australian Shepherd: American breed of dog. The Australian Shepherd, also known as the Aussie, is a breed of herding dog from the United States.
With more than 2,000 species and petals but no sepals, this flowering plant genus originated in Africa and is popular as an ornamental houseplant in cooler climates — which genus?
Begonia: Genus of perennial flowering plants.
This medium-sized antelope of India and Nepal sports corkscrew horns up to 30 inches long and a striking two-tone coat, with white around the eyes set against black face stripes — which animal?
Blackbuck: Antelope native to India and Nepal. The blackbuck (Antilope cervicapra), also known as the Indian antelope, is a medium-sized antelope native to India and Nepal.

Brachydactyly type D: Abnormal shortening of the distal part of the thumb.

Lockheed F-117 Nighthawk: American stealth ground-attack aircraft.
This age-related eye disease gradually damages the retina's central region, with a 'wet' form involving leaking blood vessels and a 'dry' form marked by deposits called drusen — what is it?
Macular degeneration: Vision loss due to damage to the macula of the eye.

Nuclear medicine: Medical specialty. Nuclear medicine (nuclear radiology) is a medical specialty involving the application of radioactive substances in the diagnosis and treatment of disease.

Osprey: Species of bird. The osprey (Pandion haliaetus), historically known as sea hawk, river hawk, and fish hawk, is a diurnal, fish-eating bird of prey with a cosmopolitan range.
Named from the Latin word for 'sparrow,' this bird order — making up over half of all species — is defined by perching feet with three toes forward and one back. What's it called?
Passerine: Perching birds of the order Passeriformes.

Peyote: Species of psychoactive cactus. Peyote, also known as Lophophora williamsii, is a small, spineless cactus which contains psychoactive alkaloids, particularly mescaline.

A member of the cashew family, this tree nut is a priority allergen, yet the world still churned out 1.4 million tonnes in 2024 — with the US, Iran, and Turkey making up 87% of it. Which green-hued nut is it?
Pistachio: Member of the cashew family. The pistachio (UK also; Pistacia vera) is a small to medium-sized tree of the cashew family.

Lacking any nervous, digestive, or circulatory system, these ancient sea-bound filter feeders pump water through pore-riddled bodies using flagella to survive — what are they?
Sponge: Animals of the phylum Porifera.
Codenamed 'Flanker' by NATO, this Soviet twin-engine fighter entered service in 1985 as an air-superiority answer to the F-14 and F-15 — what is it?

Botanically a perennial with an elongated trunk, this form isn't a single family — palms, ferns, and bamboos all independently grew tall stems to win at chasing sunlight. What is it?

A breakdown product of purine nucleotides found naturally in urine, elevated blood levels of this heterocyclic compound can trigger gout and kidney stones — what is it?
Uric acid: Organic compound. Uric acid is a heterocyclic compound of carbon, nitrogen, oxygen, and hydrogen with the formula C5H4N4O3.
Comprising the mons pubis, labia, clitoris, and vaginal opening, these external structures of the female genitalia are supplied by the pudendal arteries. What is this collectively called?
